title: AI Operations: Triage Signals, Runbooks, and Incident Response (2026)

questions.question: A MetricDeltas sample has safety_classifier_score=0.72, a cost spike, and a quality drop. Which classification does classify_incident return?
options: SAFETY with P1 severity, because the safety threshold overrides the other buckets
COST with P2 severity, because spend is the most actionable signal
QUALITY with P2 severity, because the judge score changed
TOOL_USE with P1 severity, because every mixed incident is treated as agentic
questions.explanation: The safety gate runs first and fires at 0.70 or above. It returns Category.SAFETY and Severity.P1 without letting cost or quality signals change the category.

questions.question: Incident C has tool_error_rate_delta=55 and tool_loop_detected=True. What category and severity does classify_incident select?
options: COST, P2, because a long agent loop mainly increases token spend
TOOL_USE, P1, because the loop is an agentic signal requiring immediate mitigation
QUALITY, P2, because tool errors are output regressions
SAFETY, P1, because all production side effects are safety incidents
questions.explanation: The tool bucket has the error-rate and loop signals. A detected loop upgrades the severity to P1; the runbook then adds a max_turns guard and disables the looping tool.

questions.question: For Category.COST with context_length_spike=True and feature_flag_changed=False, which conditional step appears in route_runbook?
options: Check the MCP schema and roll back the affected server
Check the safety-classifier threshold and preserve affected sessions
Check context-length p95 at the inflection point for an inlined-history prompt bug
Pin a dated model version before looking at cost telemetry
questions.explanation: The cost runbook includes the context_length_spike branch when that state flag is true. The feature-flag branch is omitted here because feature_flag_changed is false.

questions.question: In detect_silent_drift, which layer catches the sample regression while transport and cost remain clean?
options: L1 infrastructure, because the improved latency is itself an alert
L2 platform, because unchanged cost proves a token anomaly
L4 business, because the 3.5-point satisfaction drop crosses its alert threshold
L3 AI quality, through both the judge-score and output-length alerts
questions.explanation: The judge score falls about 16% and output length falls 38%, so both L3 checks fire. L1 latency improves, L2 cost is flat, and the L4 drop is below its 5-point threshold.

questions.question: A quality incident has provider_status_clean=True and model_version_changed=True. What mitigation does the quality runbook recommend?
options: Pin the model to an explicit dated version instead of the family alias
Disable every tool and reduce max_turns until the model recovers
Raise the safety threshold so fewer responses are escalated
Wait for the quarterly satisfaction survey before changing configuration
questions.explanation: After checking the provider, the model-version branch tells the responder to verify configuration and pin a dated suffix such as claude-sonnet-4-6-20260501.

questions.question: Why is a safety-classifier hit treated as P1 even when only a small number of users are affected?
options: P1 is reserved for cost spikes above 20 percent, regardless of user impact
Safety incidents are always at least P1, so scope does not lower the response priority
Safety signals are ignored until an L4 satisfaction metric confirms harm
The router cannot distinguish safety from quality and therefore defaults to P1
questions.explanation: The lesson makes safety the exception to traffic-based prioritisation: harmful or policy-violating output is always at least P1 and must reach the safety lead quickly.
